summary: PulseGuard v0.6.42 turns on signed updates: from now on PulseGuard only installs releases signed with the official PulseGuard key. It also stops flagging held or not-applicable app updates as warnings, runs the SSD retrim at most once a week, and makes the report much smaller.

sections.heading: Signed updates are now required
sections.detail: This version contains the official PulseGuard release public key. Every future update must carry a valid signature from that key, so a release published by anyone else (even from the official GitHub repository) is rejected before it is downloaded.

sections.heading: Fewer false warnings
sections.detail: App updates on a 24-hour retry hold, repeated "not applicable" offers and unknown-version packages are expected outcomes and no longer turn Fix & Optimize into a warning.

sections.heading: Faster Fix & Optimize
sections.detail: The SSD retrim/volume optimization runs at most once every 7 days, because Windows already does it weekly.

sections.heading: Smaller report
sections.detail: Healthy devices in the driver inventory keep only their name, class, status and driver details; devices with problems keep every field.

sections.heading: Fix & Optimize finishes again
sections.detail: v0.6.40 crashed while writing the final summary because the Game Ready step no longer returns CPU before/after values. The post-fix rescan and final report now run normally.
